rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Accounting #1, Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 10/26/26. (No earlier available date). Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) The codicil dated 9/13/11 stated that if "any of the above-named individuals fails to survive me," etc. Raymond Clothier survived the decedent and post-deceased. His death certificate reflects that he was also survived by a spouse. It appears that she is entitled to 1/3 of Raymond's share. [Probate Code Sect. 6401(c)(3)(A).] (2) The third amendment was not e-filed until 8/26/26, which was not at least 15 days before this hearing. Notice is defective if mailed before the filing of the pleading requiring notice. [LRSF 14.14 A.] "Filing" means when the pleading requiring notice appears on the Court's register of actions and becomes publicly viewable. Please provide a revised proposed order and courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 10/12/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B. (The papers were received after the 8/26/26 deadline, but the examiner opted to review them in hopes of being able to pre-grant this petition. If papers are not received by the deadline, and Counsel has not contacted the examiner to request more time, the hearing will ordinarily be continued automatically to the next available date. Please do not forget to show the hearing date on the first page of any pleading or cover letter. [LRSF 14.7 B.2.])

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF NEIL W. MARTIN
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Report, Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Granted per written order, although (1) there was no "second amendment" so the "First Supplement to the Second Amendment to the Petition" made no sense, (2) the administrator's verification of the "First Supplement to the Second Amendment to the Petition" verified the "Second Amendment to the Petition," which was not the pleading he verified, (3) the "First Supplement to the Second Amendment to the Petition" actually AMENDED, not merely supplemented, the proposed distribution to correct (reduce) the amount distributable to each heir, and (4) Administrator never addressed how the decedent's siblings are his heirs (the identities of the decedent's parents and their dates of death were not set forth in any verified pleading, as required by LRSF 14.18 C.3.). Because the proof of service indicated that a copy of the erroneously titled pleading was mailed to each heir, the Court will waive the irregularities so that the estate can close. The attorney of record is reminded again to review the California Rules of Court for the distinctions between the kinds of pleadings [CRC 7.3] and which ones (amendments) require notice [CRC 7.53]. NB: All pleadings must show the name and representative capacity, if any, of the party for whom the attorney is appearing, e.g., John Jones, Executor. "Petitioner" or "Respondent" alone is not sufficient. [LRSF 14.15 A.]

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF MATILDA A. ANDRES
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR PROBATE OF WILL AND FOR LETTERS TESTAMENTARY
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 11/2/26. (No earlier availability.) Issue(s) necessitating continuance: (1) Notice must be given directly to a person entitled to notice, not in care of another. A notice mailed to a person in care of another person is insufficient unless the person entitled to notice is an adult and has directed the party giving notice in writing to send the notice in care of the second person. [CRC 7.51(a).] (2) Notice of Hearing must have attached to it the procedures for how to make a remote appearance by Zoom and CourtCall, as well as information about remote public access, as set out at https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/probate-court. [LRSF 14.1 C.6.] (3) Who is Anthony Pulhin? How is he authorized to make a declaration about the will execution? (4) Who is Lawrence Andres? (5) Whose children are the husband's niece and nephews? (When did those siblings of Decedent's predeceased husband die if they also predeceased?) (6) The Proof of Subscribing Witness should have been filed separately for the record. The Attorney's Certification must be completed. (7) The family tree attached to the supplement filed on 6/30/26 does not show relationships clearly and appears to be missing the decedent. Do not respond to these issues as though answering a test, quoting the issues. Please provide just one list of all heirs and beneficiaries as they should have been listed on Attachment 8 to the amended petition, so that all heirs and beneficiaries with their relationships to the decedent, ages, and addresses are in one place. See LRSF 14.B regarding procedures for how to submit an ex parte petition (and proposed order). Deadline to provide courtesy copies of any papers filed to address these issues to the assigned examiner by 10/19/26. Examiner continuances are final and not subject to contest under LRSF 14.10 B.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF LORNA LIGUID PALANCA
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The following issues to be cleared/addressed: (1) Petitioners assert priority for appointment but do not provide supporting grounds. As issues of the predeceased spouse's parents, the petitioners' priority falls under Sec. 8461(n), which is lower than the issues of the decedent's (g) issue of brothers and sisters and (i) issue of grandparents. Also, a relative of a predeceased spouse has priority under Sec. 8461 ONLY IF the predeceased spouse would have taken any asset in this estate. However, the first supplement to the petition filed on 6/16/26 affirms that the predeceased spouse is not entitled to any part of the decedent's real property or personal property interest. Thus, the petitioners seem to have lower priority than the Public Administrator. (2) The Court may inquire about the need for probate if the decedent's only asset is an insurance policy with a designated beneficiary. (3) The declaration regarding diligent search, filed on 7/28/2026, only states that the decedent's heirs at law are unknown to the petitioners and does not describe any efforts to locate them. PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear personally or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall.
